articles.title: The Tooth That Had No Hole Yet
articles.summary: A pastry apprentice develops a white patch on a tooth and expects it to be drilled away; the dentist first asks how often he tastes syrup each day.
articles.summaryZh: 糕点学徒的牙面出现一块白斑，他以为钻掉就结束了，牙医却先问他一天尝多少次糖浆。
storyParagraphs: Pastry apprentice A-Cen did not eat whole sweets, but tasted syrup dozens of times for his master each day. When a chalky white patch appeared at the edge of a back tooth, the surface was still intact and painless. Afraid it would become a dark hole, he asked the dentist to drill immediately, believing that removing a bad place early must be cleaner.

The dentist first used a dye to reveal the film on his teeth and asked about eating frequency, cleaning, fluoride use, saliva, and earlier lesions. Microorganisms in the film used sugar and repeatedly made the local environment acidic, allowing minerals to leave the tooth surface. Between episodes, saliva and fluoride could support their return. Each taste was small, but A-Cen repeatedly interrupted the recovery interval.

The white lesion had not yet formed a cavity requiring a filling, so the dentist did not remove tooth structure immediately. Together they reduced frequent exposure, improved film removal and fluoride protection, and arranged review according to risk. Another tooth with a true cavity that could not regain its shape through mineral return received necessary restoration. Care addressed not only a visible defect but the conditions that kept creating defects.

Months later, the white patch had not vanished as if it had never existed, but it was harder, stable, and no longer enlarging. A-Cen still needed continuing care because the film, diet, saliva, and time would keep changing. One treatment could not remove the mouth from an ongoing process.

Back at the pastry shop, his master handed him the syrup spoon. After tasting the first batch, A-Cen did not leave it beside his mouth as usual. He washed it and placed it upside down between tastings.
storyParagraphsZh: 糕点学徒阿岑每天并不吃整块甜点，却要替师傅尝几十次糖浆。他在一颗后牙边缘发现粉白斑时，牙面仍完整，也不疼。阿岑怕它变成黑洞，要求牙医立刻钻掉，觉得坏的地方越早挖走越干净。
牙医先用染色剂显出牙面薄膜，又问进食频率、清洁、含氟用品、唾液和既往病变。糖被薄膜里的微生物利用后，局部会反复变酸，矿物从牙面离开；两次之间，唾液和氟又能帮助矿物回来。阿岑每次只尝一点，却让修复的间隔不断被打断。
白斑尚未形成需要填补的洞，牙医没有立刻去除牙体。她和阿岑一起改变频繁暴露，改善薄膜清洁和含氟防护，并按风险复查；另一颗已经出现空洞、无法靠矿物恢复形状的牙，则接受必要修复。处理对象不只是眼前的缺口，也包括让缺口持续发生的条件。
几个月后，白斑没有消失得像从未存在，却变硬、稳定，也没有继续扩大。阿岑仍需长期维护，因为薄膜、饮食、唾液和时间会继续变化。一次治疗不能让口腔从此脱离过程。
回到糕点房后，师傅递来糖勺。阿岑尝过第一锅，没有像往常那样把勺留在嘴边，而是把它洗净，倒扣在两次试味之间。
articles.conceptName: Dental caries as a biofilm-mediated process
explanationParagraphs: Dental caries is a dynamic, biofilm-mediated process in which ecological change under conditions such as frequent fermentable carbohydrate exposure produces acid and shifts the balance toward demineralization over remineralization. Early non-cavitated lesions may be arrested or reversed through risk control, biofilm removal, fluoride protection, and monitoring; cavitated lesions may require restoration. It is not caused by one bacterium or one sweet and cannot be managed by filling holes alone.
explanationParagraphsZh: 龋病是牙面生物膜在频繁可发酵碳水等条件下发生生态变化，产生酸并推动脱矿超过再矿化的动态过程。早期未成洞病变可能通过控制风险、清洁生物膜、含氟防护和监测得到阻止或逆转；已形成空洞时可能需要修复。它不是单纯由一只细菌或一次吃糖造成，也不能只靠填洞解决。

articles.title: The Tooth That Always Met First
articles.summary: A musician receives a new crown that appears correct in a still bite, yet during meals it always takes the force before the other teeth.
articles.summaryZh: 琴师换上一颗新牙冠，静静咬住时看似合适，一开口吃饭，那颗牙却总比其他牙先承受力量。
storyParagraphs: Musician Shen Xian cracked a back tooth and received a new crown after treatment. The dentist asked him to bite blue paper, which showed several orderly marks, and Shen did not feel that the crown was very high. At home, however, it struck first during meals. By the next day the tooth felt sore, and he was clenching his jaw while practising.

At review, the marks remained unremarkable when Shen closed gently. The dentist asked him to move forward and side to side and observed chewing, joints, muscles, and night-time habits. The crown was only slightly high in the still position, but blocked a movement path that should have been shared and guided by several teeth. Repeated loading began to irritate the supporting tissues and muscles.

The dentist adjusted only a confirmed interference rather than grinding broadly to create an attractive blue-paper pattern. She also checked the cracked tooth, joint, and muscles for other problems, because facial pain and headache cannot all be assigned to tooth contact. Shen did not need equally dark marks everywhere; he needed contacts and guidance suited to him in stillness and movement.

After adjustment, soreness gradually declined. Shen also addressed his habit of clenching while playing and returned for review. Crown material, supporting tissues, and adaptation change over time; one mark cannot represent every future load.
Before his next performance, he bit through a small piece of dry bread. The new crown did not make the first light click. He returned the rest to its paper bag and began tuning his strings.
storyParagraphsZh: 琴师沈弦的一颗后牙裂了，修复后戴上新牙冠。牙医让他咬住蓝纸，纸上留下几个整齐印点，沈弦也说不算高。可回家吃饭时，那颗牙总先撞上，第二天便发酸，练琴时还不自觉地咬紧下颌。
复诊时，沈弦平静合牙，印点仍不显眼。牙医让他缓慢前伸和左右移动，又观察咀嚼、关节、肌肉和夜间习惯。牙冠在静止位置只高一点，却在侧向运动中挡住了本应由多颗牙共同引导的路线，反复受力后，牙周和肌肉都开始抗议。
牙医只调整确认过的干扰处，没有为了追求一张‘漂亮’的蓝纸大面积磨牙。她也检查裂牙、关节和肌肉是否另有问题，因为脸痛和头痛不能一概归给牙齿接触。沈弦需要的不是所有牙同时留下同样深的点，而是在静止和运动中获得适合他的接触与引导。
调整后，牙齿的酸痛逐渐减轻。沈弦还改了练琴时咬紧的习惯，并接受复查；牙冠材料、牙周状态和适应会随时间变化，一次印记不能代表以后所有负荷。
下一次演出前，他咬断一小块干面包。新牙冠没有抢先发出那声轻响，他把剩下的面包放回纸袋，开始给琴弦调音。
explanationParagraphs: Occlusion describes relationships between upper and lower teeth in static contact and jaw movement, involving supporting tissues, muscles, temporomandibular joints, restorations, and neural adaptation. Assessment requires more than one bite-paper mark and must consider movement, loading, symptoms, and individual function. Contact abnormalities may matter but are not the sole cause of all facial pain; adjustment needs a clear diagnostic basis and should preserve tooth structure.
explanationParagraphsZh: 咬合描述上下牙在静态接触和下颌运动中的关系，并涉及牙周、肌肉、颞下颌关节、修复体与神经适应。评估不能只看一次咬纸印记，还要结合运动、受力、症状和个体功能。接触异常可能相关，却不是所有面部疼痛的唯一原因；调整应有明确诊断依据，并尽量保存牙体。

articles.title: A Tooth's Fourth Repair
articles.summary: Each small defect at an old filling leads to a complete larger replacement; by the fourth repair, less natural tooth remains than filling.
articles.summaryZh: 每次旧填充边缘出一点问题，牙医都把它整块换成更大的，第四次时，留下的真牙已经比填充更少。
storyParagraphs: Merchant Lu Ming received a filling in a back tooth when young. Years later, a small corner broke at its edge, and a second dentist removed the entire filling and replaced it with a larger one. After that, every stain, worn area, or small crack led to another complete replacement. Lu assumed that new was always more reliable and never asked how much natural tooth left with each repair.

At the fourth visit, a fine defect appeared along one side of the restoration, while the tooth had no clear symptoms. Lu again requested complete replacement. A young dentist reviewed imaging, examination, and history and assessed whether disease was active along with cleaning and dietary risks. Repeatedly expanding the boundary, she explained, would eventually approach the pulp or weaken the remaining tooth toward deeper fracture.

Once the defect was confirmed, only the failed edge was repaired and the sound portion remained. Another early lesion received risk control and monitoring rather than drilling for appearance alone. A cavity or structure unable to maintain function would still receive necessary restoration, but actual need would determine removal rather than a rule to replace everything.

Lu improved cleaning and fluoride protection and returned at a shorter initial interval. Conservative care did not mean doing less and then ignoring the tooth, nor did it promise every lesion would heal itself. Prevention, remineralization, sealing, repair, and necessary restoration formed one long maintenance path.

At the end, only a small fragment of old material lay on the tray. Remembering the silver piece nearly half a tooth in size from his first replacement, Lu asked the dentist to place this sliver in a paper envelope for him.
storyParagraphsZh: 商人陆明年轻时补过一颗后牙。几年后，填充边缘掉下一小角，第二位牙医把旧填充全部挖出，换了一块更大的。此后每逢变色、磨损或小裂口，修补都从头重做。陆明觉得新东西总比旧东西可靠，从未问每次带走多少真牙。
第四次就诊时，旧填充一侧出现细小缺损，牙齿本身尚无明显症状。陆明照例要求全换。年轻牙医看过影像、探查和既往记录，又评估病变是否活动、清洁与饮食风险。她指出，若每次都扩大边界，修复循环迟早会逼近牙髓或让牙体裂得更深。
缺损经过确认后，只修补了失效边缘，仍可靠的部分被保留；另一处早期病变先接受风险控制和监测，没有因为颜色不好看就立刻钻开。若病变已经成洞或结构不能维持功能，仍会做必要修复，但去除范围由实际需要决定，而不是由‘全部换新’决定。
陆明同时改善清洁和含氟防护，缩短最初复查间隔。保守处理不是少做之后不管，也不是承诺所有病变都能自行恢复；它把预防、再矿化、封闭、修补和必要修复放在同一条长期维护路径上。
治疗结束时，托盘里只有一小片被取下的旧材料。陆明想起第一次补牙时那枚接近半颗牙大的银块，便请牙医把这一小片也放进纸袋带走。
explanationParagraphs: Minimal intervention dentistry emphasizes early detection, risk control, prevention, and preservation of sound tooth structure. Controllable early lesions may receive non-operative or micro-invasive care, and suitable defective restorations may be repaired rather than automatically replaced. Necessary restoration remains available, but lesion activity, cleanability, structure, and patient needs guide the least invasive effective intervention, supported by long-term review of disease and the restorative cycle.
explanationParagraphsZh: 微创牙科学以早期发现、风险控制、预防和保存健康牙体为核心，对可控制的早期病变优先采取非手术或微创措施，对失效修复体在合适时修补而非必然整块更换。它不排斥必要修复，而是按病变活动、可清洁性、结构和患者需要选择最小有效干预，并通过长期复查管理疾病与修复循环。

articles.title: The Headache That Rested on Sundays
articles.summary: A printing apprentice has weeks of headache and nausea, blamed on overwork until a doctor asks why it always improves on Sundays.
articles.summaryZh: 印刷学徒连续数周头痛恶心，大家都说是赶工过劳，直到医生问起为什么星期日总会好一些。
storyParagraphs: After rushing a winter catalogue, printing apprentice Xiao Pu experienced weeks of headache, fatigue, and nausea. The first clinician saw his long hours and attributed the symptoms to overwork, advising rest. Two nights of sleep did not resolve them, but Xiao noticed that Sundays away from the workshop were consistently better.

At the next visit, the physician did not remain with the first answer. She first checked for danger signs needing urgent action, then considered infection, migraine, medication, vision, workplace exposure, and other possibilities according to likelihood and consequence. Xiao mentioned that the apprentice beside him also felt dizzy and that symptoms worsened several hours after the furnace started. Those two clues moved the workplace higher.

Inspectors found the exhaust pipe blocked by paper scraps, allowing a colourless combustion gas to remain indoors. A canary near the window being well proved little because its location and exposure differed. More useful evidence came from several people becoming ill in one place, improving away from it, and a site measurement supporting the same explanation. The furnace was stopped and the room ventilated and repaired.

The physician still arranged follow-up. Finding a plausible cause did not erase every alternative. Failure to improve or dangerous change would require reassessment. The reasoning process was not a long list of memorized diseases but continued comparison, exclusion, prioritization, and updating as evidence arrived.
On the first Monday after the repair, Xiao worked until afternoon without headache. He removed a wall notice reading 'Keep windows closed during rush work' and exposed the blackened vent behind it.
storyParagraphsZh: 印刷学徒小浦赶制冬季书单后，连续几周头痛、乏力和恶心。第一位接诊者见他常熬夜，认为是过劳，嘱咐休息。小浦睡了两晚仍旧难受，却发现每到不进工坊的星期日，症状会轻许多。
再次就诊时，医生没有只守着第一个答案。她先排查需要立即处理的危险征象，再把感染、偏头痛、药物、视力、工作暴露和其他可能按概率与后果列在心里。小浦说同桌学徒最近也常头晕，而症状总在开炉几小时后加重，这两条新信息让工坊环境被推到前面。
检查工坊的人发现排烟管被纸屑堵住，燃烧产生的无色气体滞留室内。窗边的一只金丝雀没有生病证明什么，人和动物所处位置、时间都不同；真正有用的是多人同地发作、离开后改善以及现场检测共同指向同一解释。工坊立即停用炉子并通风检修。
医生仍安排随访，因为找到一个合理原因不代表其他可能自动消失。小浦若未改善或出现危险变化，需要重新评估。判断过程不是把所有疾病背成一张长清单，而是在新证据到来时比较、排除、排序并更新。
修好排烟后的第一个星期一，小浦在工坊待到下午也没有头痛。他撕下墙上那张‘赶工勿开窗’的纸条，露出后面已经发黑的通风口。
explanationParagraphs: Differential diagnosis develops plausible alternatives for the same symptom or sign, prioritizes them by danger and likelihood, seeks discriminating evidence from history, examination, and tests, and updates their order as information changes. It prevents premature closure without requiring an endless list of rare diseases. A working diagnosis needs reassessment and safety-netting because early evidence is incomplete and more than one cause may coexist.
explanationParagraphsZh: 鉴别诊断针对同一症状或体征形成一组合理候选，结合危险程度、常见程度、病史、检查与检验寻找有区分力的证据，并随新信息更新排序。它既防止过早锁定第一个解释，也不等于无限罗列罕见病。工作诊断应配合复评与安全网，因为早期证据不完整，多个原因也可能同时存在。

articles.title: One Hundred and Twenty Red Slips
articles.summary: After screening ten thousand symptom-free workers, a port issues 120 positive red slips and an official immediately announces 120 patients.
articles.summaryZh: 港城筛查一万名无症状工人后发出一百二十张阳性红纸，官员立刻宣布找出了一百二十名病人。
storyParagraphs: Fearing the arrival of a rare lung disease, a port screened ten thousand symptom-free dock workers. The test was good at finding people who truly had the disease and had a low false-alarm rate among healthy people. One hundred and twenty workers received red slips. That day, the port official announced 120 patients and prepared to close every warehouse where they worked.

The physician requested confirmation first. Very few people in the city had the disease. Even a small false-positive proportion among healthy workers produced many red slips when applied to nearly ten thousand healthy people. Most genuine cases could be detected, but their starting number was small. A positive screen changed probability without turning directly into a certain diagnosis.

After clinical history, imaging, and more targeted testing, only a little over ten recipients were confirmed and the others left isolation. Screening had still been useful: it reduced ten thousand people to 120 needing further assessment. The error was treating the screening exit as the diagnostic endpoint while ignoring how likely disease had been in the tested group beforehand.

The port changed its process. A positive report now stated the intended population, underlying disease frequency, test performance, and next step instead of showing colour alone. High-risk, symptomatic, and general screening groups received different interpretations because the same result had different meaning from different starting points. Warehouse closure waited for clinical confirmation and public-health judgement.

The next screening round printed more red slips. The official did not count them and issue an order. He placed the first in a wooden frame marked 'awaiting confirmation' and waited for the physician to open the second door.
storyParagraphsZh: 港城担心一种罕见肺病传入，便给一万名无症状码头工人做初筛。检验很擅长找出真正患病者，对健康者也有很低的误报率。结果一百二十人拿到红纸，港务官当天宣布已经发现一百二十名病人，准备关闭他们所在的全部仓库。
医生要求先做确认检查。城里当时真正患病的人极少，即使健康者只有很小比例被误报，放到近一万名健康人中也会产生不少红纸。相反，真正患者虽大多能被检出，人数本来就少。初筛阳性改变了可能性，却没有把它直接变成确定诊断。
后续病史、影像和更有针对性的检验完成后，红纸中只有十余人被确认，其余人解除隔离。初筛仍然有价值：它把需要进一步检查的人从一万人缩到一百二十人；错误在于把筛查出口当作诊断终点，并忽略受检人群原先有多大可能患病。
港城修改流程，报告阳性时同时写明适用人群、疾病出现频率、检验性能与下一步，不再只给一个颜色。高风险、有症状和普通筛查人群分别解释，因为相同结果在不同起点上含义不同。仓库关闭也等待临床确认和公共卫生判断。
下一轮筛查又打印出红纸。港务官没有数纸便下令，他把第一张夹进标着‘待确认’的木框，等医生打开第二道门。
explanationParagraphs: Base-rate reasoning in diagnosis combines a test result with the tested population's probability of disease before testing. Even with high sensitivity and specificity, a small false-positive rate applied to many healthy people can make false positives a large share of positive results when disease is rare. Bayesian updating, likelihood ratios, and confirmation pathways translate test performance into an individual's post-test probability.
explanationParagraphsZh: 诊断中的基础率推理要求把检验结果同受检人群在检验前的患病可能结合。即使敏感度和特异度都较高，在疾病罕见的低风险人群中，少量误报乘以大量健康者，也可能让阳性结果中假阳性占很大部分。贝叶斯更新、似然比和确认流程帮助把检验性能转换为个体检验后的概率。

articles.title: The Patient Missing from the Paper
articles.titleZh: 论文里没有的那位病人
articles.summary: A young physician follows a famous study, but a patient who climbs ladders for work bears a cost the paper never asked about.
articles.summaryZh: 年轻医生照着一篇著名研究开出治疗，病人却因每天必须爬梯工作，最先承受了论文没有问过的代价。
storyParagraphs: Roofer Old Qi visited a clinic for a chronic condition. A young physician had just read a large study in which a treatment reduced future complications on average and prescribed accordingly. The study was rigorous, but the physician did not ask that Qi climbed ladders dozens of times each day or explain common harms and other options.

Days later, dizziness kept Qi from work and nearly made him fall from a low ladder. Rather than continuing blindly or stopping forever on his own, he returned. The physician reread the study and found that its participants, follow-up, and main outcomes did not perfectly match Qi. Absolute benefit behind the average relative improvement also depended on Qi's starting risk. The evidence was not wrong, but it could not finish this decision by itself.

A senior physician helped them examine study quality, guidelines, and alternatives alongside Qi's health, past responses, work, costs, and goals. Qi cared most about reducing long-term risk while working safely until his daughter's wedding. They discussed benefits, harms, and uncertainty, chose a more suitable adjustment, and agreed on observation and review.

The young physician stopped using 'supported by research' as a full stop. Different questions required different evidence, which still needed assessment for bias, applicability, and meaningful outcomes. Clinical expertise helped interpretation and implementation; the patient's values and circumstances determined which reasonable option was acceptable. Resources and feasibility also belonged inside the room.

When Qi returned to work, his daughter's wedding invitation sat in his breast pocket with the next review date written on its back. He stood for a moment on the first rung of the lowest ladder before passing his tools up to the roof.
storyParagraphsZh: 屋顶匠老齐因慢性病来到诊所。年轻医生刚读完一篇大型研究，某种治疗平均能减少未来并发症，便照着结论开了方案。研究写得严谨，医生却没有问老齐每天要爬几十次梯子，也没有说明常见不良反应和其他选择。
几天后，老齐因头晕停工，差点从低梯上跌下。他没有擅自继续或永久停药，而是回到诊所。医生重新看研究，发现试验人群、随访时间和主要结局同老齐并不完全一样，平均相对改善背后的绝对收益也取决于他原先风险。证据没有错，却不能自己完成这次决定。
资深医生同他们一起核查研究质量、指南和其他方案，再结合老齐的身体情况、既往反应、工作、费用与目标。老齐最看重的是既降低长期风险，又能在女儿婚礼前继续安全工作。他们讨论收益、伤害和不确定性，选了更适合的调整，并约定观察与复评。
年轻医生以后不再把‘有研究支持’写成句号。不同问题需要不同证据，研究也要看偏倚、适用性和结局是否重要；临床经验帮助解释和实施，病人的价值与处境则决定多种合理选择中哪一种值得接受。资源和可行性也不能被留在诊室门外。
老齐复工那天，胸前口袋里放着女儿婚礼的请柬，背面写着下次复诊日期。他在最低一架梯子的第一格站了一会儿，才把工具递上屋顶。
explanationParagraphs: Evidence-based medicine integrates the best current research evidence with clinical expertise and the patient's values, goals, and circumstances. It is not mechanical obedience to one paper or guideline. Bias, effect size, absolute risk, applicability, meaningful outcomes, uncertainty, and feasibility require assessment. Evidence helps define options and consequences; individualized decisions are completed through professional interpretation and patient participation.
explanationParagraphsZh: 循证医学把当前最佳研究证据、临床专业判断和患者的价值、目标与具体处境结合起来。它不是机械照搬一篇论文或指南；还要评估研究偏倚、效应大小、绝对风险、适用性、重要结局、不确定性与可行性。证据帮助界定选择及其后果，个人化决策则通过专业解释和患者参与完成。

articles.title: Every Number Was Still Below Its Line
articles.titleZh: 每个数字都还没有越线
articles.summary: No single night-shift reading triggers an alarm, but a nurse sees breathing, pulse, urine output, and behaviour all moving in the same direction.
articles.summaryZh: 夜班病人的每项读数都没有单独触发警报，护士却看见呼吸、脉搏、尿量和神情正朝同一方向变化。
storyParagraphs: Postoperative patient Uncle Chen was joking at the start of the night shift. At two in the morning, temperature, pulse, and breathing each remained below its individual warning line, so the trainee proposed waiting for the morning round. Nurse Ye Ning remembered four hours earlier: breathing had quickened with each check, pulse kept rising, urine output fell, and answers came more slowly.

She repeated the measurements, checked the equipment, and reviewed skin, pain, wound, medication, and fluid balance. When the changes were combined in an early-warning chart, the score required escalation. More importantly, both the trend and Ye's judgement that 'he is not the same as earlier' were worsening. She followed the escalation process and called senior staff without waiting for one number to turn red.

Review found a developing complication. The team treated it and increased monitoring before the patient became more unstable. At the later meeting, success was attributed neither to intuition alone nor to a score alone. Baseline observation, repeated measurement, trends, structured scoring, clinical judgement, and a clear response pathway had worked together.

The ward improved handover so usual state and recent change travelled between shifts, not just the latest reading. Suspect devices were checked, but possible error could not justify indefinite delay. Concerns from patients and families also entered observation. An alert had to reach someone who responded, and records had to show what action followed.
At dawn, Ye used a red pencil to join four points that had not individually crossed their lines. The rising slope was more visible than any isolated number.
storyParagraphsZh: 术后病人陈伯在夜班开始时还能说笑。凌晨两点，他的体温、脉搏和呼吸都仍在表格单项警戒线以内，值班实习生便说可以等晨查。护士叶宁却记得四小时前的样子：呼吸一次比一次快，脉搏持续上升，尿量变少，回答问题也慢了。
她重新测量并核对设备，又查看皮肤、疼痛、伤口、用药和出入量。把几项变化合在早期预警表上后，分数已要求升级；更重要的是，病人的趋势和叶宁对‘他不像刚才那个自己’的判断都在恶化。她按流程呼叫高年资人员，没有等某一个数字终于变红。
复查发现正在发展的并发症，团队及时处理并提高监测频率。若再晚几小时，病人可能更加不稳。事后会议没有把成功归给护士的直觉，也没有只归给评分表：基线观察、重复测量、趋势、结构化评分、临床判断和清楚的升级路径共同发挥作用。
病房随后改善交接，让班次之间传递平时状态和近期变化，而不只是最后一个读数。设备异常先复核，但不能用‘可能测错’无限拖延；病人和家属提出的异常也进入观察。警报触发后必须有人回应，记录也要能看出行动是否发生。
天亮时，叶宁在记录纸上把四个尚未越线的点用红铅笔连起来。那条向上的斜线，比任何一个孤零零的数字都醒目。
explanationParagraphs: Early warning through clinical observation uses baseline state, repeated vital signs, trends, overall appearance, and structured scores to detect deterioration and connect triggers to explicit escalation and response. One normal item cannot cancel several coordinated changes, while a score cannot replace clinical judgement. Verification, handover, patient or family concern, timely reassessment, and closed-loop action determine whether warning actually protects the patient.
explanationParagraphsZh: 临床观察与早期预警通过基线状态、重复生命体征、趋势、整体表现和结构化评分识别恶化，并把触发结果连接到明确升级与响应。单项正常不能排除多项共同变化，评分也不能替代临床判断。测量复核、交接、患者或家属担忧、及时复评和闭环行动共同决定预警是否真正保护患者。

articles.title: Beginning Again for the Seventh Time
articles.summary: An older patient retells her history in every new room; six carers work diligently, yet an overlooked test result belongs to no one.
articles.summaryZh: 老人每到一个新诊室都重新讲病史，六位照护者各自认真，漏掉的化验结果却一直没有主人。
storyParagraphs: Aunt Lin lived with several chronic conditions. After a winter admission, she met a ward physician, clinic physician, pharmacist, home nurse, and rehabilitation therapist. Each worked carefully, yet she told her history from the beginning for a seventh time. A medicine stopped at discharge still appeared active on an old list, and no one was named to review a newly ordered follow-up test.

A week later, the home nurse found both old and new medicine sets on Lin's table. She thought the clinic had reconciled them; the clinic assumed the discharge team would follow up; the laboratory sent an abnormal result to an unattended old account. Lin returned to hospital unwell. No one person had ignored everything. Information, relationship, and management had each broken a little at every transition.

The hospital named a coordinator who built an updateable care plan with Lin. Current medicines, reasons for stopping others, pending tests, owners, appointments, and warning signs were explicit. A sending team confirmed that the receiving team understood each handover, and a pharmacist reconciled medication. Lin and her daughter could view the plan and flag errors.

She still saw several professions because complex care could not belong to one person alone. One clinician familiar with her long-term goals maintained the relationship, while interventions followed the same plan. Transfer of responsibility named a person and time. A task did not end merely because a document had been sent; results needed acknowledged review.

At the next new consultation, Lin began, 'I should start seven years ago.' The physician had already opened the plan. 'Last time we stopped at your breathlessness on the stairs,' she said. Lin slowly folded the old medicine list in her hand.
storyParagraphsZh: 林姨患有几种慢性病，冬天一次住院后，先后见过病房医生、门诊医生、药师、家庭护士和康复师。每个人都很认真，她却要第七次从头讲起。出院时停掉的一种药在旧清单上仍显示使用，新开的复查化验则没有写明由谁查看结果。
一周后，家庭护士发现林姨桌上摆着新旧两套药。她以为门诊已经核对，门诊以为出院团队会随访，化验室只把异常结果发到一个无人值守的旧账户。林姨因不适再次入院。问题不在某个人完全失职，而在信息、关系和管理在每次交接处都断了一小段。
医院为林姨指定一名协调者，同她一起整理一份可更新的照护计划。当前用药、停药原因、待办检查、负责者、预约和危险信号都清楚写出；交接由发送方确认接收方已理解，药师进行用药核对。林姨和女儿也能查看并指出错误。
此后，她仍会见不同专业人员，因为复杂照护不可能由一人包办。但有一位熟悉她长期目标的人保持关系，各项治疗也围绕同一计划衔接。若责任转移，会明确到姓名和时间；结果没有被确认前，任务不会因为文件发出就自动结束。
下一次进入新诊室，林姨刚准备说‘我从七年前讲起’，医生已经打开计划说：‘上次停在您走楼梯会喘这里。’她把握在手里的旧药单慢慢折了起来。
explanationParagraphs: Continuity of care makes care coherent across time, professions, and settings through informational, relational, and management continuity. Shared updateable records, explicit ownership, medication reconciliation, closed-loop results, reliable handovers, and an ongoing relationship familiar with patient goals reduce repetition, omission, and conflict. Continuity does not require one person forever; it requires information and responsibility to survive change.
explanationParagraphsZh: 照护连续性使患者跨时间、专业和机构获得连贯照护，通常包括信息连续、关系连续和管理连续。共享且可更新的记录、明确责任、用药核对、闭环结果、可靠交接和熟悉患者目标的持续关系，可减少重复、遗漏与冲突。连续并非要求永远由同一人照护，而是变化发生时信息和责任不会断裂。

articles.title: The Conversation That Began After the Signature
articles.summary: A tailor signs a form outside the procedure room; only when a nurse asks how she will work afterward does she discover that the paper omitted what mattered most to her.
articles.summaryZh: 裁缝在手术室门外签完表格，直到护士问她术后怎样工作，她才知道纸上漏掉了自己最在意的问题。
storyParagraphs: Tailor Mia was scheduled for an elective procedure. That morning, a staff member gave her a page of dense text in the corridor, said, 'The doctors have arranged everything,' and pointed to the signature line. Mia was unfamiliar with the medical language and believed refusal might endanger future care, so she signed without asking questions.

During preparation, a nurse casually asked who would cover Mia's work during recovery. Mia then learned that a common recovery limitation could prevent fine hand work for weeks, just as she was completing the town's wedding-season orders. She did not know about other reasonable options, consequences of delay, or the option of no intervention. The nurse paused the process because a name on paper did not demonstrate understanding or voluntariness.

The later conversation used familiar language and diagrams. Clinicians explained the purpose, likely benefits, material risks, alternatives, and uncertainty, asked what mattered to Mia, and invited her to describe her understanding in her own words. She had time to consult family, could refuse or change her decision, and would not be punished for questions.

Mia chose another reasonable option first and delayed the original plan until her orders were complete, with a route for reassessment if circumstances changed. She neither simply obeyed the physician nor received technical responsibility alone. Professional evidence and her values met in one decision. The signature documented only part of a process and could not replace it.
Before leaving, Mia drew a line through the old signature. Weeks later, she returned with a new form covered in questions and signed its final page only after the conversation.
storyParagraphsZh: 裁缝米娅要接受一项可择期治疗。当天清晨，工作人员在走廊递给她一页密字表格，说‘医生都已经安排好了’，便指向签名处。米娅对医学用语不熟，也以为不同意就会失去以后看诊机会，于是没有提问便签了名。
准备过程中，护士随口问她恢复期谁替她做活。米娅这才得知某种常见恢复限制可能让她数周不能精细用手，而她正要完成全镇婚礼季的订单。她还不知道有其他合理方案、推迟的后果和不处理的选择。护士停下流程，因为纸上的名字没有证明她理解或自愿。
之后的谈话使用她熟悉的语言和图示。临床人员说明建议目的、可能收益、重要风险、替代方案与不确定性，也询问米娅最看重什么，并请她用自己的话讲回理解。她有时间同家人商量，可以拒绝或改变决定，不会因提问受到惩罚。
米娅最后选择先采用另一项合理方案，把原计划延后到订单结束，并约定若情况变化如何复评。这个选择不是简单听从医生，也不是把技术判断全丢给患者，而是让专业证据和她的价值在同一决定里相遇。签字只记录过程的一部分，不能替代过程。
离开前，米娅在旧表格的签名上划了一条线。数周后，她带着已经写满问题的新表回来，谈完以后才在最后一页重新签名。
explanationParagraphs: Informed consent is a voluntary and revisable decision by a patient with decision-making capacity after receiving and understanding relevant purpose, benefits, material risks, alternatives, and the option of no intervention; it is not a signed form. Shared decision-making integrates best evidence and clinical judgement with patient values and circumstances when reasonable options exist. Communication support, checking understanding, sufficient time, and freedom from pressure are part of the process.
explanationParagraphsZh: 知情同意是具备决策能力的患者在获得并理解相关目的、收益、重要风险、替代方案和不处理选择后，自愿作出并可改变的决定；它不是一张签名表。共同决策在存在合理选择时，把最佳证据、临床判断与患者价值和处境结合。沟通支持、理解核查、足够时间和免受压力都是过程的一部分。

articles.title: After the Threshold Was Lowered
articles.summary: A director demands that a new test miss no patient; after its threshold is lowered, almost every case is found and the review clinic fills with healthy people.
articles.summaryZh: 院长要求新检验一个病人也不能漏掉，门槛降低后，真正患者几乎都被找到，复查室却挤满了健康人。
storyParagraphs: A laboratory developed a test with a continuous reading. People with disease usually had higher values and those without disease lower ones, but the two groups overlapped slightly. Afraid of missing treatable cases, the director ordered a very low positive threshold. Nearly every true case was caught, along with many healthy people who received review notices.

When queues filled the review clinic, the director demanded, 'Stop accusing healthy people,' and raised the threshold. False alarms fell, but some genuine patients with lower readings passed beneath it. The technologist placed both rounds side by side. Where values overlap, moving one line usually trades one type of error for another.

They separately calculated the proportion of diseased people detected and the proportion of non-diseased people correctly excluded, without mixing the denominators. In initial screening, the cost of a miss might justify a threshold favouring detection followed by targeted confirmation. In confirmation or before potentially harmful treatment, the cost of a false alarm might weigh more heavily.

Threshold selection therefore stated purpose, target population, reference standard, and follow-up pathway and reported uncertainty. Even with both measures fixed, the proportion of positive people who truly had disease changed with disease frequency in the tested group. Test accuracy was not itself clinical benefit; access, workflow, and consequences also required evaluation.
The technologist kept two movable lines on the transparent chart, one marked SCREEN and the other CONFIRM. The director no longer asked for them to be painted into one.
storyParagraphsZh: 实验室开发出一种连续读数的检验，患病者通常较高，健康者通常较低，两群数字却有一小段重叠。院长担心漏掉可治疗病例，命人把阳性门槛降得很低。真正患者几乎都被拦下，许多健康人也收到复查通知。
复查室排起长队后，院长又要求‘别再冤枉健康人’，把门槛抬高。误报明显减少，一些读数较低的真实患者却从门下走了过去。实验师把两轮结果并排放好：在两群读数重叠时，移动同一条线通常会用一种错误换取另一种错误。
他们分别计算患病人中有多少被检出，以及无病人中有多少被正确排除，不再把两个分母混在一起。用于初筛时，漏诊代价较高，可以选择更偏向发现的门槛，再用更有针对性的检查确认；用于确认或可能带来有害治疗时，误报的代价又可能更大。
门槛选择因此写明用途、目标人群、参照标准和后续路径，并报告不确定性。即使两个指标固定，阳性者中真正患病的比例还会随受检人群患病频率改变；检验准确性也不等于临床获益，流程、可及性和后果必须一起评估。
实验师最终在透明图板上保留了两条可移动的线，一条标‘筛查’，一条标‘确认’。院长没有再要求把它们涂成同一条。
explanationParagraphs: Sensitivity is the proportion of people with disease who test positive; specificity is the proportion without disease who test negative. For continuous measures, changing the threshold often raises one while lowering the other, so purpose and the consequences of misses and false alarms guide selection. Neither directly equals the probability that an individual's positive or negative result is correct, which also depends on prevalence, likelihood ratios, and pre-test probability.
explanationParagraphsZh: 敏感度是在真正患病者中检验呈阳性的比例，特异度是在真正无病者中检验呈阴性的比例。连续指标改变阈值时，提高一项常会降低另一项，选择取决于用途及漏诊、误报的后果。两者不直接等于阳性或阴性结果对个人的可信度，后者还受患病率、似然比和检验前概率影响。

articles.title: The Doctor Who Saw Every Shadow
articles.titleZh: 看见每一道影子的医生
articles.summary: After missing one faint lesion, an imaging physician begins calling every grey shadow abnormal and soon fills the review clinic with diseases that are not there.
articles.summaryZh: 影像医生漏看一处极淡病灶后，开始把所有灰影都判成异常，很快又让复查室堆满了并不存在的疾病。
storyParagraphs: Imaging physician Gu Qing once missed an extremely faint lesion. Although the patient later received treatment, the review stayed with her. Afterward, she labelled nearly every ambiguous image abnormal. Misses fell, but follow-up imaging and biopsies rose quickly; many shadows proved to be overlapping tissue, motion, or equipment artefact.

When an unnecessary investigation caused a complication, Gu became afraid of false alarms and tightened her reporting threshold. Weeks later, another genuine but faint change passed unnoticed. She had not first become better and then worse at reading images. Her decision criterion had moved back and forth between two kinds of consequence.

The department inserted cases with known outcomes into routine reading and separately counted detections, misses, false alarms, and correct rejections. It distinguished how separable the images were from a reader's willingness to call abnormality. Better acquisition, less motion, comparison with old images, and second reads could separate true change from background; instructions to be merely bolder or more cautious only moved the criterion.

Different settings still used different strategies. Screening, emergency care, and pre-treatment confirmation attached different costs to misses and false alarms. Disease frequency, downstream test risk, and available resources also changed decisions. When certainty was not possible, the report could state uncertainty and recommend an appropriate next step instead of forcing every grey shadow into immediate yes or no.

Later Gu encountered another image with a remaining doubt. She neither circled it in red as a diagnosis nor erased it. She wrote 'compare with prior image and obtain second review' beside it and moved the film to the double-reading rack.
storyParagraphsZh: 影像医生顾青曾漏看一处极淡病灶。虽然病人后来得到治疗，那次复盘仍让她不安。此后每逢模糊影像，她宁可全部标成异常。漏诊少了，复查和穿刺却迅速增加，许多影子最后只是重叠组织、运动或设备杂纹。
一次无谓复查让病人承受了并发症，顾青又开始害怕误报，判读门槛随之变严。几周后，一处真正但很淡的变化再次被放过。她发现自己不是先后变得更会看图，而是在两种后果之间来回移动判断标准。
科室把已知结果的病例混入日常读片，分别统计发现、遗漏、误报和正确排除，并把影像本身的可分辨程度同医生愿意报异常的倾向分开。改善扫描质量、减少运动、比较旧片和双人复核，能让真实变化与背景更容易分开；单纯要求‘大胆些’或‘谨慎些’只会移动门槛。
不同场景仍使用不同策略。筛查、急诊和治疗前确认的漏诊与误报代价并不相同，疾病出现频率、后续检查风险和可用资源也会改变决定。无法确定时，可以明确写出不确定性并安排合适下一步，而不是强迫每道灰影立刻变成是或否。
后来顾青遇到一张仍有疑点的片子。她没有用红笔圈成确诊，也没有擦掉它，只在旁边写下‘同旧片比较，并请第二人复核’，然后把片子移到双读架上。
explanationParagraphs: Signal detection examines decisions when signal and noise overlap, separating discriminability from the decision criterion. Lowering a criterion usually increases both detections and false alarms; raising it reduces false alarms while potentially increasing misses. The suitable position depends on prior probability and consequences of both errors. Better data quality, repeated observation, and independent review can improve discrimination rather than merely move the threshold.
explanationParagraphsZh: 信号检测研究在信号与噪声重叠时怎样作判断，区分可辨别能力与决策门槛。降低门槛通常增加发现也增加误报，抬高门槛则减少误报也可能增加遗漏；合适位置取决于先验概率和两类错误的后果。改善数据质量、重复观察和独立复核可提升辨别，而不只是移动标准。

articles.title: Twelve Thermometers That Agreed and Were Wrong
articles.titleZh: 十二支一起读错的温度计
articles.summary: Twelve clinic thermometers agree with one another until they and their drifting master thermometer meet an external reference.
articles.summaryZh: 诊所的十二支温度计彼此读数一致，直到它们同一支已经漂移的主温度计一起接受外部标准检验。
storyParagraphs: A community clinic owned twelve electronic thermometers. Each month, nurses placed them in a water bath beside the master thermometer kept in a cabinet. If they differed little, each received an approval label. The twelve instruments always agreed, so clinicians trusted every decimal place.

A year later, an external quality visit brought a traceable reference system. The master thermometer read nearly one degree high at several temperatures. Because the everyday instruments had always followed it, all were biased high together. For months, some people had been labelled febrile incorrectly, while other trends were obscured by the shared error. Agreement had not kept the instruments on the true scale.

A technician recorded each instrument's state before adjustment, compared it at several points covering its working range, stated error and measurement uncertainty, and then adjusted, repaired, or withdrew it. Temperature, humidity, drops, ageing, and batteries could affect stability, so check intervals followed risk and performance history rather than one annual point.

The clinic retained routine quality controls to reveal sudden change, while formal comparison connected measurements to a reference with documented traceability. Adjustment could not erase earlier error, so affected records required review. Instruments leaving the workshop carried as-found and as-left results, validity date, and applicable range.
The old master thermometer was not discarded. The technician removed its gold MASTER label and replaced it with red paper: reads 0.8 degrees high; not for clinical use.
storyParagraphsZh: 社区诊所有十二支电子温度计。护士每月把它们同柜里的主温度计放进同一水槽，只要相差不多便盖上合格标签。十二支仪器总是彼此一致，医生因此十分信任那些小数点后的数字。
一年后，外部质量检查带来可追溯的标准装置。主温度计在几个温度点都高读近一度，十二支日常温度计因为一直追随它，也一起偏高。过去数月，一些人被错误标为发热，另一些趋势则被这个共同偏差遮住。仪器没有互相争吵，却共同离开了真实尺度。
技术员记录每支仪器调整前的状态，在覆盖实际使用范围的多个点比较，说明误差和测量不确定性，再按结果调整、维修或停用。温度、湿度、跌落、老化和电池都会影响稳定，检查间隔因此依据风险和历史表现决定，不再一年到头只看一个点。
诊所还保留日常质量控制，用来发现突然变化；正式比较则连接到有证据链的参考标准。调整并不抹去过去的错误，受影响记录要被评估。每次仪器离开维修室，也标明调整前后结果、有效日期和适用范围。
那支旧主温度计最后没有被扔掉。技术员摘下它的金色‘主表’标签，换上一张红纸：高读零点八度，禁止临床使用。
explanationParagraphs: Measurement calibration compares an instrument's indications with a reference of known uncertainty and traceability over stated conditions and range, establishing the relationship between indications and reference quantity values. Adjustment may follow but is not calibration itself. Intervals should reflect purpose, risk, drift, and performance history, with as-found and as-left states recorded. Agreement among instruments does not prevent common bias away from the correct scale.
explanationParagraphsZh: 测量校准是在规定条件和范围内，把仪器示值同具有已知不确定性和可追溯性的参考标准比较，建立示值与参考量值之间的关系；调整是可能的后续动作，不等同校准本身。周期应依据用途、风险、漂移和历史表现确定，并记录调整前后状态。多台仪器彼此一致，也可能共同偏离正确尺度。

articles.title: The First Note to Sound Again
articles.summary: After illness, a pianist's right hand reaches only one key; someone promises a new brain route will restore everything, while the therapist begins with one shirt button.
articles.summaryZh: 钢琴师病后右手只能落在同一只琴键上，有人许诺换条脑路便可复原，治疗师却先让他扣好一颗纽扣。
storyParagraphs: After illness, pianist He Wen's right hand moved slowly and all five fingers often landed on the same key. A seller of a new treatment promised that the brain would simply open another route if He repeated whole pieces often enough. He practised until his arm hurt, but the notes remained crowded together and he began avoiding the piano.

A rehabilitation therapist assessed impaired and retained abilities and asked about daily goals. He most wanted to button his shirt, hold a cup, and play three bars for his daughter's birthday. Training began with movements that were achievable but challenging, repeatedly practising relevant finger separation, touch, grasp, and release with timely feedback and rest. Tasks changed gradually so success did not belong only to one exercise table.

The following weeks contained both improvement and plateaus. Some function came from reorganization and strengthening within affected networks, some from compensation through different movements. Fatigue, sleep, pain, attention, lesion location, and time constrained learning. The therapist never promised unlimited rewiring and did not blame a plateau on insufficient will.

He later buttoned his clothes, steadied a cup, and carried that control back to the keys. Practice intensity, meaning, and feedback changed with performance, while the team prevented excessive repetition from causing pain or reinforcing poor movement. Change depended on experience, but not every experience produced the desired change.
On his daughter's birthday, he did not play the whole old piece. His right hand pressed one note alone, paused, then added the second and third. He lifted his hand without chasing the fourth.
storyParagraphsZh: 钢琴师贺闻病后，右手动作变得迟缓，五指常一起落在同一只琴键上。一名推销新疗法的人说，大脑会自己另开道路，只要反复弹整首曲子，很快就能恢复。贺闻练到手臂疼，声音仍挤成一团，也开始躲开钢琴。
康复治疗师先评估受损、保留的能力和日常目标。贺闻最想自己扣衬衫、端杯子，并在女儿生日时弹出三小节旋律。训练从能成功又有挑战的动作开始，反复练习同目标相关的手指分离、触碰和抓放，给予及时反馈，也安排休息。任务逐渐变化，避免只会在治疗桌上完成一种动作。
数周里有进步，也有平台。某些功能来自受影响网络重新组织和加强，某些来自其他动作的补偿；疲劳、睡眠、疼痛、注意、病变位置和时间都会限制学习。治疗师从未承诺大脑能无限改写，也不把停滞归咎于意志不够。
贺闻后来能独立扣衣、稳住杯子，再把这些控制带回琴键。练习的强度、意义和反馈随表现调整，团队也防止过度重复造成疼痛或强化错误动作。变化依赖经验，却不是任何经验都会带来想要的变化。
女儿生日那晚，他没有演奏整首旧曲。右手先单独按下一音，停了一拍，又接上第二和第三音。贺闻抬起手，没有追赶第四音。
explanationParagraphs: Neuroplasticity is the nervous system's capacity to change connections, activity, and functional organization through learning, experience, injury, and environment, providing an important basis for rehabilitation. Change is task- and context-specific and constrained by dose, repetition, salience, feedback, rest, injury, and individual conditions; maladaptive change can also occur. It supports potential improvement but does not guarantee full recovery or justify blaming the patient for incomplete recovery.
explanationParagraphsZh: 神经可塑性是神经系统因学习、经验、损伤和环境而改变连接、活动与功能组织的能力，是康复学习的重要基础。变化具有任务和情境特异性，受训练剂量、重复、意义、反馈、休息及损伤和个体条件限制，也可能形成不理想适应。它支持改善的可能，却不保证完全恢复，更不能把未恢复归因于患者不够努力。

articles.title: The Staircase That Had Only Seven Steps Left
articles.summary: A dancer's foot has healed, but the theatre stairs remain as steep as on the day of her fall; each avoidance makes the seven steps harder to approach.
articles.summaryZh: 舞者的脚伤已经愈合，剧院楼梯却仍像事故那天一样陡，她每次避开它，那七级台阶便更难靠近。
storyParagraphs: Dancer Jian Qiu injured her ankle falling on the theatre stairs. After the bone injury healed, she could walk on level ground, but her heart raced and leg stiffened at those seven steps. She used the rear freight lift and avoided even similar stairs. Months later, strength and confidence had both declined, and her return to the stage kept moving away.

The therapist first confirmed physical status and actual safety. He neither forced her to rush to the top nor merely said, 'Do not be afraid.' Together they ranked situations by Jian's own expectations: standing at the stairs, touching the rail, stepping onto the first stair, moving up and down two, and eventually completing all seven under different lighting and with people passing. She agreed to each step and repeated it long enough to gain new experience.

On her first step, Jian predicted that she would fall; she experienced fear and mild discomfort but remained upright. The therapist did not require every sensation to disappear before progress, nor treat all pain as danger or all pain as irrelevant. New physical signs prompted reassessment. Familiar alarm responses were recorded alongside the difference between expected and actual outcomes before difficulty increased.

Training was not simply one more stair each day. It involved approaching previously avoided cues, reducing unnecessary safety behaviours, and learning within tolerable limits that the feared outcome was not inevitable. Progress fluctuated, and order changed with sleep, stress, and goals.

On opening night, Jian crossed backstage toward the final seven stairs. At the top, she noticed that her right hand had held the rail throughout. She did not return to repeat them. Just before stepping onto the stage, she released the rail.
storyParagraphsZh: 舞者简秋从剧院楼梯摔伤脚踝。骨伤愈合后，她能在平地行走，却每到那七级台阶便心跳加快，腿也发僵。她改走后门货梯，连看见相似楼梯都绕开。几个月后，脚力和信心一起下降，重返舞台的日期不断推迟。
治疗师先确认身体状况和实际安全，没有强迫她一次冲上顶，也没有只说‘别怕’。他们把困难情境按简秋自己的预期排开：先站在楼梯口，再触碰扶手、踏第一阶、上下两阶，最后在不同光线和有人经过时走完整段。每一步都由她同意，并重复到能获得新经验。
第一次踏阶时，简秋预言自己会跌倒，实际只是紧张和轻微不适。治疗师不要求感觉完全消失才继续，也不把疼痛一概视为危险或一概忽略。若出现新的身体征象，计划会复核；若只是熟悉的警报反应，他们记录预期与结果之间的差异，再逐渐增加难度。
训练不是简单每天多走一级。关键在于接近原先回避的线索，减少依赖不必要的安全动作，并在可承受范围内学习‘害怕的结果并非必然发生’。进度有反复，顺序也会按睡眠、压力和目标调整。
首演那晚，简秋从后台走向最后七级。到了顶端，她才发现右手一直扶着栏杆。她没有回去重走，只在踏上舞台前，把手从栏杆上松开。
explanationParagraphs: Graded exposure collaboratively and progressively approaches feared and avoided situations, sensations, or activities after suitability and safety are assessed. Repeated experience updates threat predictions and restores function. It is not coercion, vague reassurance, or mechanical dose escalation, and anxiety need not disappear first. Hierarchy, pace, and safety behaviours should follow individual goals while real danger remains distinguished from excessive alarm.
explanationParagraphsZh: 分级暴露在确认适合和安全后，以协作方式逐步接近被恐惧和回避的情境、感觉或活动，通过重复经验更新威胁预期并恢复功能。它不是强迫、泛泛安慰或机械加量，也不要求焦虑先完全消失。层级、节奏和安全行为应针对个体目标调整，并持续区分实际危险与过度警报。

articles.title: Only a Faint Line on the Scan
articles.summary: A porter's back pain lasts six months while imaging shows only a common mild change; one clinician says nothing is wrong, another says he must never lift again.
articles.summaryZh: 搬运工的腰痛持续半年，影像只见常见轻微改变；一个医生说没什么，另一个人却说他再也不能搬东西。
storyParagraphs: Porter Ma Liang had back pain for six months after a strain. Imaging showed only a common mild change. One clinician said, 'There is nothing there,' leaving Ma feeling that his pain was denied. Hearing about the image change, his foreman concluded that lifting would further damage his spine and removed him from the job, cutting his income in half.

Poor sleep, worry, and prolonged inactivity left Ma increasingly stiff. He feared bending, while household debt made pain harder to bear. The rehabilitation team neither assigned everything to the scan nor called the pain imaginary. They reassessed physical problems requiring care and asked about sleep, mood, beliefs, family support, and work demands, examining how these factors interacted to sustain symptoms and disability.

The plan included suitable physical care and progressive return to activity, while addressing sleep and fear and working with the foreman on initial loads, pace, and shared lifting. Ma learned to distinguish warning signs of injury from familiar pain that did not necessarily indicate new damage, and the team monitored responses and adjusted when needed. No single item received the title of the real cause.

Months later, the scan was no prettier, but Ma walked farther, slept better, and resumed part of his work. Improvement did not prove biology irrelevant or that thought alone could resolve all pain. It showed that bodily, psychological, and social conditions interact in health experience and that treatment goals include function and life.
On his first day back, a crate stood at the edge of the quay. Ma neither tried to prove himself alone nor turned away. He called a colleague, and they lifted one side each onto a low trolley.
storyParagraphsZh: 搬运工马良扭伤腰后，疼痛持续了半年。影像只见一道常见的轻微改变，第一位医生说‘没什么’，马良觉得自己的痛被否认；工头听说影像有变化，又认定他再搬货就会损坏脊柱，把他调离工作，收入也少了一半。
失眠、担心和长时间不活动让马良越来越僵。他害怕弯腰，家里欠款又使每天的疼痛更难承受。康复团队没有把一切归给影像，也没有说痛只是想出来的。他们重新检查需要处理的身体问题，同时询问睡眠、情绪、信念、家庭支持和工作要求，寻找这些因素怎样相互维持症状与失能。
计划包括适合的身体治疗和逐步恢复活动，也处理睡眠与恐惧，并同工头调整最初的重量、节奏和协作方式。马良学习区分损伤警讯与不一定代表新伤害的熟悉疼痛，团队则持续观察反应，必要时修改。没有哪一项单独被称为真正原因。
数月后，影像没有变得更漂亮，马良却能走得更远、睡得更好，也恢复部分工作。进步并不证明生物因素不重要，也不证明所有疼痛都能靠改变想法解决；它表明人的健康经历会由身体、心理和社会条件相互作用，治疗目标也应包括功能与生活。
复工第一天，一只箱子放在码头边。马良没有独自逞强，也没有转身避开。他叫来同伴，两人各抬一边，把箱子放上矮车。
explanationParagraphs: The biopsychosocial model treats biological processes, psychological experience and behaviour, and social relationships and environment as interacting influences on health. It supports a mechanism-informed whole assessment rather than dividing symptoms into physical or imagined. Their relative importance differs by problem and connections require evidence. Care may address bodily, cognitive-emotional, behavioural, and social conditions and evaluate symptoms, function, and patient goals together.
explanationParagraphsZh: 生物心理社会模型把生物过程、心理体验与行为、社会关系和环境视为相互作用的健康因素，用于形成机制明确的整体评估，而不是把症状简单分成‘身体的’或‘想出来的’。不同问题中各因素权重不同，联系需要证据。干预可同时针对身体、认知情绪、行为和社会条件，并以症状、功能与患者目标共同评价。
